statement.text:
E1-K1 complete-state cap kernels: exact-head review of 940f0ad0. Primary: results note 6c1bf004. This review rests on all 42 artifacts, one per path changed against approved 3a40d2c5. Verdict: approved, as a measurement delivery. The broader E1 matrix stays open.

What I checked
- Scope: git diff 3a40d2c5..940f0ad0 touches only experiments/, the retained evidence and three notes. There is no change to src, package.json or npm-shrinkwrap.json, so no runtime, profile or API change.
- Recomputed statistics: I parsed node-timing.json and chromium-timing.json directly.
  - Each has 1,911 rows (21 fixtures × 13 operations × 7), and every operation has exactly 7 samples.
  - The at-cap admitSuccessor and queryCaptureAndValidate median, minimum and maximum, for all seven families in both environments, equal the note's two tables exactly. For example, ledger admit in Node is 26.03 [24.38–27.68] and in Chromium 66.1 [45.0–75.3].
- statistics.json records referenceEquality true, 27 strict controls and 28 wire refusals per environment, 7 samples and 2 warmups, and states its method (no trimming, gates or reruns).
- Kernels (experiments/complete-state-cap/kernels.ts):
  - admitSuccessor is action-schema validation, then the supported fold, then state-schema validation on an effective result, from an admitted predecessor. That is as described.
  - queryCaptureAndValidate is structuredClone(state), query-parameter validation, evaluate, then result validation. That mirrors S1's Folder.query state path.
  - Wire kernels return {refused:'wire_size'} only for that error code and rethrow everything else. So the 196 refusal spans are labelled, and the note keeps them apart from successful encodes.

Architecture: sound methodology, and the claims are honestly scoped.
- These are warm single-call kernels from a prepared predecessor; source loading, fixture building and warmups are outside the clock.
- There is no subtraction of medians to attribute stages, and no extrapolation.
- Near-cap medians exceeding at-cap ones are not claimed as a trend.
- Refusal durations are not presented as successful large-state work.
- The note shows that size alone does not predict cost (scalar 13 versus primitive-array 32,765 token charges). It also shows that ineffective duplicate-ID folds still scan complete state.

Security: no runtime change. Strict controls confirm that no state over 128 KiB, no 1,001-row table and no 121-character text is accepted.

Simplification
- The recommendations are right and minimal: keep complete state with V0, S1 and checkpoints as the default, and start no effects prototype.
- Investigate repeated full walks and copies only for a concrete application, with a separate equivalence review.

Note (not blocking): every near-cap and at-cap state is legal under the 128 KiB state cap, yet exceeds the 64 KiB single-block CBOR limit. That is fine today, because archives replay state rather than storing it. But any future checkpoint or state export must use the chunked byte framing (P4) for state payloads, never a single native block. The note says this and should keep saying it.

statement.text:
P3-F1 L1 successor: exact-head re-review of 0d6eebce against my review 564e5046. Primary: tombstone results note ea2d55b9. This review rests on all 45 artifacts, one per path changed against 3a40d2c5. Verdict: approved.

What I ran. I used a scratch clone at 0d6eebce with npm ci and a build, on Node 26.10.0.
- My original L1 probe, policy {rows: 50}, distinct create/delete cycles:
  - at ff4a30c4 it wedged at generation 99 with 49 markers;
  - it now completes 200 cycles (generation 400) with 0 deletion markers left.
- My pinned variant:
  - pin g1 holding history/p = [7], delete p, then advance three generations;
  - the pinned generation reads [7] and the current generation reads undefined, so the marker after a retained live value survives;
  - after release and one more commit, history/p is fully gone (0 history rows, 0 markers);
  - accounting ends at exactly the 4 live rows and 96 bytes.
- tests/local-generations.test.ts passed, and npm run check passed.
- I did not rerun Chromium. The IndexedDB change is the same rule, checked by reading the code.

Architecture: sound.
- Both pruneKey (SQLite) and the IndexedDB collect apply one rule in a single ordered pass: keep a version only if it is visible to some kept generation, and either is live or follows a retained live value.
- A leading marker equals absence for every read (row and page select at or before id), so reads are unchanged.
- A marker after a retained live value is kept, which is necessary while an older pin sees that value.
- It sits in the same transaction and accounting path as before, and ordinary retirement still visits only keys changed in the previous generation.

Security: no change in trust surface.
- This remains raw local storage with no authority.
- The fix removes a deterministic self-wedge (permanent quota) that ordinary churn could trigger.

Simplification: none needed. The fix is a few lines, mirrored in both adapters. The earlier minor point (sharing the page byte arithmetic) remains optional.

Full P3 stays open, as the note says.

T1-H1 package test isolation: exact-head review of 4be60f1b. Primary: results note 77bebea8. This review rests on all 27 artifacts, one per path changed against approved fc8e2093. Verdict: approved.

What I ran. I used a scratch clone at 4be60f1b with npm ci and npm run setup, on Node 26.10.0.
- I ran tests/package.test.ts in parallel (--test-concurrency=4) with all three browser test files (browser-sessions, identity-evidence-browser, native-proof-browser), which are the race the change fixes.
- 17/17 passed, and dist/src/integrity/browser.js still exists afterwards. The test's own sentinel and adapter assertions passed, so the shared dist survived the staged production build.
- Source scope: only tests/package.test.ts and the new tests/helpers/package-build.ts. The production build, package, approvals and runner are unchanged.

Architecture: sound and minimal.
- The real cause (npm run build removes the shared dist while parallel Vite tests resolve #atseq-integrity from it) is removed by building and packing in a private copied root with the unchanged production commands.
- The fresh consumer stays separate.
- The test now proves its own guarantee:
  - a unique sentinel file in the shared dist and the unchanged browser integrity adapter bytes are asserted after the build;
  - the deterministic red run, with cwd set back to root, retains the ENOENT failure;
  - the staged build's provenance sourceHashes are checked against the original checkout files;
  - outputHashes are checked against the installed consumer.
- The hidden-lock finding is correct and well handled. npm's node_modules/.package-lock.json is trusted only when it is newer than the package directories. Copying its unchanged bytes last keeps the source installation's metadata cache valid. The staged tarball then matches the original 12,172 paths exactly, which the file-list comparison records.

Security: no change to the integrity checks.
- Both the staged build and the fresh consumer verify the copied and installed dependency trees.
- verbatimSymlinks keeps .bin links relative inside the stage and never follows them out.
- The sentinel is removed in finally.

Simplification
- Copying the whole installed toolchain is the simplest correct route; there is no second install or partial closure.
- Two non-blocking robustness points:
  1. The fixed copy list (scripts, src, lexicons, docs, README, CONTRIBUTING, LICENSE and so on) must track package.json "files" and the build inputs. If a future packaged path is added only to "files", the stage would silently omit it. Cheap guard: assert that every package.json "files" entry exists in the stage before packing, or derive the list from "files" plus the fixed build inputs.
  2. The test now needs an existing dist/src/integrity/browser.js in the checkout, because it reads it before building. Before, it built dist itself. That is fine under CI's setup step, but say so in the test comment or the contributing notes, so that "npm test" on a fresh clone fails clearly rather than with a bare ENOENT.
- When integrating with the pending OAuth candidate, keep its packed-consumer tampering case, as the note says.
